Welcome
As Headteacher of St Walburga’s School, I would like to take this opportunity to welcome you. I hope that our website gives you a brief insight into the life of our school – and I encourage you to visit us to find out more. Originally founded in the town centre in the 1870s, St Walburga’s School is the longest established Catholic primary school in Bournemouth. The school moved to its current site in 1929 and we continue to welcome children and families from all over Bournemouth to join our ‘School Family’.

pageCache.pageTitle: St Walburga's Catholic Primary School - Before and After School clubs
pageCache.text:
Before and After School clubs
The Before and After school Club is run by St Walburga’s Catholic Primary School and exists to provide high quality out-of-school hours childcare for our parents. It provides a range of stimulating and creative activities in a safe environment.
The club operates from 7.30 am - 8.30am and from 2.50pm – 5.45pm term time only.
All parents must complete a registration form for each child attending the club and sign an agreement to adhere to the club policy.
· Only children attending St Walburga’s Catholic Primary School are eligible to attend the Club
· All places are subject to availability - please enquire at the school office.
· The registration process must be completed through the school office prior to the child’s commencement at the club
· Non-contracted pupils are welcome to use the club provided there are spaces and parents/carers have previously completed the registration process
Arrival and Departure
Parents/carers are required to bring their child directly to the club and sign them in. You should enter the club via the Key Stage 1 playground, and staff will be alerted to your arrival when you press the club doorbell situated on the Reading Den.
Children will be escorted onto the relevant playground at 8.40am by the club staff.
Reception, Year 1 and Year 2 children will be collected from their classroom by a member of club staff. KS2 children will come to the club from their classrooms.
The staff will take a register of all contracted children and will liaise with the school office immediately to determine any reason why a child is not accounted for.
When a child is collected at the end of or during a session, they must be signed out by a parent/carer and the time recorded.
Parents/carers must ensure that any person who may collect their child is listed on the registration form and that it is kept fully up to date.
Parents must inform club staff if their child is going to be absent from club, either via the Club mobile or via the school office. If they are phoning to inform the school that their child is going to be absent from school, they must also inform the office if their child is due to attend club.
7.30am – 8.30am- parents bring their children to Before School Club situated in the club room where a range of activities are set out.
8.00am - children wishing to have breakfast wash their hands and are offered a range of food.
8.20am - tidy up time, encouraging children to take responsibility for the club environment.
8.30am - children collect their coats and bags. Both KS1 and KS2 children are escorted to their appropriate playground where they join the rest of the children awaiting the start of school.
2.50pm – 2.55pm – children go to club, register is taken
3.45pm (approx.) - children will be offered a snack and a drink
Children will be offered a range of play and planned activities, indoors and outdoors.
5.45pm—children MUST be collected by 5.45pm at the latest.
Once registered to the school club, parents will be charged for every day their child is registered to attend. For example, if their child is registered for a place on a Monday and Tuesday, those days of the week will be reserved for them, and they will be charged for every Monday and Tuesday for the half term ahead. In order to pay, they will be invoiced, in advance, for the upcoming half term. Parents will then need to go on WisePay to pay the amount owed. Payment will need to be made within 30 days of the date of invoice. There is an option for using childcare vouchers.
We can only register a certain number of children per day so you may have to join a waiting list. Please contact the school office and they will be able to let you know if we have places or if we currently have a waiting list.
The current cost of this provision (September 2026) is £11.50 per session for the After School Provision, and £4.50 per session for Breakfast Club.
A charge will be levied for late collection. A fee will be applied from 5.45pm onwards at £1 per minute per child. This charge will be invoiced by the school office directly.

pageCache.text:
Sports Premium
We are incredibly proud of the high-quality Sport and Physical Education provision at St Walburga's Catholic Primary School. We believe that every child should have the opportunity to flourish through physical activity, developing the skills, confidence and enjoyment needed to lead healthy, active lives.
Sport and PE are a vital part of both our curriculum and wider enrichment offer. We provide a broad range of opportunities for all pupils to participate, compete and succeed, both within the school day and through our extensive programme of extracurricular clubs, festivals, competitions and sporting events.

pageCache.pageTitle: St Walburga's Catholic Primary School - Learning Values
pageCache.text:
Learning Values
In the first half of the Autumn Term, we think about what being respectful means to us and how we can show respect towards ourselves and others. We display some of our ideas in our classrooms.
In Autumn 2, we look at how we can be collaborative in our school, our community, and the world.
Throughout Spring 1, we look at what being honest means to us - we think about how important it is to tell the truth and how we can be honest in our learning.
In Spring 2, we look at the learning value 'Brave'.
In Summer 1, we explore our learning value 'Compassionate'.
In Summer 2, it is 'Independent'.
